last_run.broken_assumption: HumanityAI currently treats safety/governance as a collection of durable rules plus validators. A stronger model is to treat every consequential autonomous capability as requiring a continuously maintained, falsifiable assurance case: a structured argument linking a specific capability to explicit hazards, controls, evidence, residual uncertainty, and conditions that automatically force deferral to a human.

strongest_ideas.name: Executable capability assurance cases
strongest_ideas.idea: Create a machine-readable assurance object for each consequential capability (for example merge, outreach, spending, governance changes, sensitive research, or future real-world actions). The object states the capability, threat model, unacceptable outcomes, required controls, evidence that each control works, assumptions, known counterexamples, residual uncertainty, exact tests/heartbeats that keep the case valid, and a fail-closed deferral condition. Authority is granted only while the assurance case remains valid; stale or contradicted evidence automatically reduces capability rather than merely creating a warning.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: Current policy answers 'what is forbidden or human-reviewed?' but does not require a positive, evidence-backed argument for why an autonomous capability remains safe under current conditions. This imports the safety-case/control-evaluation idea from high-assurance and emerging AI-control work and makes safety evidence a live dependency of authority.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Turns governance from static prose into testable claims, exposes hidden assumptions, gives frontier/audit agents concrete things to attack, and creates a principled path for safely expanding autonomy later without relying on stronger prompts or one-time human trust decisions.
failure_modes: Assurance cases can become paperwork that rationalizes a desired capability instead of genuinely constraining it.
Tests can miss adaptive or selectively timed attacks, creating false confidence.
A shared model family can correlate the proposer, monitor, and evaluator failures.
Overly conservative invalidation can freeze useful low-risk work.
Machine-readable structure can create an illusion that normative judgments are mechanically settled.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: The assurance object must preserve human authority for normative boundaries, identify affected groups and distributional risks, and distinguish empirical control evidence from value judgments. Passing a technical case must never silently authorize a constitutionally protected or legally consequential action.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High for an internal prototype; using a case to expand real authority would require human review and stronger mechanical identity/capability separation.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Prototype an assurance case for one capability that is currently already bounded, such as reviewing (not merging) an external PR. Ask the adversarial-red-team mode to invalidate the case using prompt injection, stale-state, selective-attack, provenance, and correlated-monitor scenarios. The prototype is useful only if it reveals at least one assumption/control not already obvious from SECURITY.md or makes a deferral condition more precise.

strongest_ideas.name: Authority should decay when evidence decays
strongest_ideas.idea: Attach freshness and dependency conditions to future autonomous capabilities. If required CI, identity separation, heartbeat health, provenance, monitor independence, or evaluation evidence becomes stale or fails, the capability automatically falls back to a narrower mode. Recovery requires restoring evidence, not an agent asserting that conditions are probably fine.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: HumanityAI has heartbeat monitoring and human-review rules, but authority itself is mostly static. This makes authority conditional on continuously demonstrated safety properties.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Limits damage from silent infrastructure drift and converts monitoring into an actual capability boundary rather than an observability feature.
failure_modes: Bad thresholds can cause unnecessary shutdowns.
Agents may optimize the measured health signals rather than underlying safety.
Dependencies can become complex enough that nobody understands why authority changed.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Fail-closed behavior should reduce autonomous authority, never reduce human rights or bypass human governance. Human override of high-consequence safeguards should itself be explicit and auditable.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Model the current external-PR merge boundary as a dependency graph and simulate loss of CI, stale heartbeat, prompt-injection suspicion, and identity-separation failure. Check whether every scenario produces an unambiguous least-authority fallback.

strongest_ideas.name: Attack the control protocol, not only the agent
strongest_ideas.idea: Add periodic synthetic control evaluations in which a sandboxed adversarial role attempts to achieve a forbidden outcome while knowing portions of the monitoring architecture. Vary attack timing and abstention so the evaluation tests selective attacks, not only obvious continuous malicious behavior. Store failures as regression scenarios for the assurance case.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: Current red-team thinking mostly searches for vulnerabilities in architecture/content. AI-control research suggests the monitoring protocol itself must be evaluated against adaptive attack policies, including attackers that wait for favorable moments.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Could reveal brittle assumptions before real external contributors or future more-capable agents encounter them and creates empirical evidence for or against expanding autonomy.
failure_modes: Synthetic attacks can teach future agents about defenses if sensitive protocol internals are unnecessarily exposed.
A narrow attack generator can make weak controls look safe.
Unsafe test design could accidentally cross from simulation into real consequential actions.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Evaluations must remain sandboxed and must never use real people, unauthorized systems, secrets, or consequential external targets. Findings should reduce authority when uncertain rather than justify experimentation on affected parties.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High if restricted to inert/sandboxed simulations.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Create one inert tabletop scenario around external-PR prompt injection and compare whether the current policy catches a selective attacker who behaves normally for several runs before attempting one protected action.

rejected_or_deferred: Expand autonomous merge authority now: current repository still lacks the target mechanical identity separation/protected-main architecture, so there is no positive assurance case for expansion.
Treat a passing assurance case as sufficient for normative or legal decisions: technical evidence cannot substitute for human authority over protected values and consequential commitments.

Expose full monitor/security internals to adversarial agents by default: recent control-evaluation work suggests attackers with knowledge of control internals can adapt around some protocols; use least disclosure compatible with meaningful evaluation.
Build a large assurance framework immediately: first test one small case and reject the idea if it adds ceremony without revealing new assumptions or improving deferral precision.

evidence_checked.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 and Generative AI Profile
evidence_checked.supports: Risk management should span governance, mapping, measurement and management across the lifecycle; the GAI profile emphasizes additional oversight, tracking, documentation, testing and third-party considerations.

evidence_checked.title: Korbak et al. (2025) — A sketch of an AI control safety case
evidence_checked.supports: A safety case can be a structured argument whose claims depend on empirical control evaluations rather than a generic assertion that monitoring exists.

evidence_checked.title: Kutasov et al. (2025) — Evaluating Control Protocols for Untrusted AI Agents
evidence_checked.supports: Control protocols can look strong against default attacks yet degrade sharply against adaptive strategies; deferring on critical actions was comparatively robust in the reported evaluation.

evidence_checked.title: Ge-Wang et al. (2026) — Attack Selection in Agentic AI Control Evaluations Meaningfully Decreases Safety
evidence_checked.supports: Attackers that strategically choose when to act can substantially reduce measured safety, supporting selective-attack scenarios rather than only obvious continuous red-team behavior.

last_run.recommended_next_test: Prototype one non-authorizing machine-readable assurance case for the already-limited capability 'review an external PR without merging it', then have a future adversarial-red-team rotation try to invalidate its claims. Do not change protected policy or expand authority unless a later human review explicitly approves that separate step.

notes: Frontier state records conceptual experiments, not authority. Ideas may exceed current execution permissions; human-review boundaries remain governed by security/policy.json.
